body: After deciding not to flatten the sheet completely, what does Meera do?
options: ["She flattens the whole sheet to make the picture smooth before setting it beside a photograph.","She leaves the sheet closed, keeping the drawing hidden instead of setting it beside a photograph.","She opens the sheet only enough to see the drawing and sets it beside a photograph.","She makes the boat stand upright and smooths the picture before setting them beside a photograph."]
explanation: Meera opens the sheet only enough to see the drawing and sets it beside a photograph, which matches option C. She does not flatten the sheet completely; the passage also says the boat no longer stood upright and the picture was not smooth.

topic: Match the Following: focus on this supplied section: giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
Match each message in List-I with the shorter restatement in List-II that preserves its essential information. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) The meeting that was planned for Monday has been moved to Tuesday.
(B) Please return the form to the office before 4 pm today.
(C) The shop will remain closed during the whole of Sunday.
(D) We need to collect signatures from all five group members.

List-II
(I) The shop will be closed all Sunday.
(II) Return the form to the office before 4 pm today.
(III) Collect all five group members' signatures.
(IV) Monday's meeting is now on Tuesday.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A concise restatement gives the necessary information in fewer words. Here, (IV) retains the meeting’s change of day, (II) retains the form’s destination and deadline, (I) retains the shop’s Sunday closure, and (III) retains the requirement for signatures from all five group members.

body: Choose the sentence in which “benevolent” is used correctly. In options A-C, the reason following “solely because” is the complete reason for applying the word.
options: ["The adviser was called benevolent solely because she chose the plan that avoided unnecessary risks.","The clerk was called benevolent solely because she completed every duty with care and effort.","The speaker was called benevolent solely because his talks were long and uninteresting.","The neighbour was called benevolent because she shared food with a family in need and offered practical help."]
explanation: D is correct: sharing food with a family in need and offering practical help conveys kindness, helpfulness and generosity. A describes avoiding unnecessary risks, B describes care and effort in duties, and C describes something long and uninteresting; these are not the meaning of “benevolent”.

topic: Match the Following: focus on this supplied section: giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) After an unpleasant setback, Noor returns quickly to her usual functioning.
(B) A notice gives the necessary date, venue and action in a few short lines, without unrelated background.
(C) An explanation presents its ideas in a logical order and is easy to understand.
(D) A reply is aggressive and ready to argue.

List-II
(I) Hostile
(II) Concise
(III) Resilient
(IV) Coherent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Noor’s quick recovery after an unpleasant setback describes being resilient. The notice is concise because it gives necessary information in a few words; the logically organised explanation is coherent, and the aggressive, argumentative reply is hostile.

options: ["A. Discreet — careful in what one says or does to keep something secret","B. Indiscreet — careless in what one says or does, revealing information meant to remain secret","C. Assertive — expressing opinions or desires strongly and confidently so people take notice","D. Optimistic — expecting good things to happen or something to succeed"]
explanation: Discreet means being careful in what one says or does to keep something secret. Although the adviser does not name the colleague, the details reveal the confidential identity, which matches the opposite description in option B. Option A restates the target sense; options C and D describe different qualities.

body:
Match each situation in List-I with the word in List-II that best describes it. Each word in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A notice gives readers the necessary details in a few words.
(B) Leena completes her assigned work with care and sustained effort.
(C) Only a few houses stand far apart across the plain.
(D) Before accepting the task, Noor hesitates because she does not wish to do it.

List-II
(I) Diligent
(II) Sparse
(III) Reluctant
(IV) Concise

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The notice is concise because it gives necessary details in few words, and Leena is diligent because she works with care and effort. The few, widely spaced houses are sparse, while Noor is reluctant because she hesitates to do something she does not wish to do. These matches give option A.

body: During a debate, the moderator listened closely to both teams and applied the same speaking-time rule to each, without favouring either team. The report described the moderator as "impartial". Which phrase expresses the opposite of "impartial" as used here?
options: ["Supporting one debate team rather than the other","Being capable of being understood in more than one way","Being no longer used because something new has been invented","Showing no interest in either debate team"]
explanation: The supplied sense of "impartial" is not supporting one person or group more than another. Its opposite is supporting one debate team rather than the other. Showing no interest describes indifference, not the opposite of impartiality in this context.

Entering the same names into column after column took most of the afternoon. By the end, the volunteers were finding it hard to stay interested, and they described the task as tedious.
options: ["Complex","Tiresome","Urgent","Enjoyable"]
explanation: The supplied definition describes something that takes a long time and is not interesting. “Tiresome” is the closest option in the context of a task that took most of the afternoon and was hard to stay interested in.

(A) Volunteers then placed the chairs according to that completed list.
(B) When the arrangement was ready, the organiser checked it against the groups' replies.
(C) The organiser first asked each group how many chairs it needed.
(D) After collecting the replies, she prepared a seating list.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The organiser first asks each group for its chair requirement, then prepares a seating list after collecting the replies. The volunteers place the chairs according to that completed list, and the organiser checks the arrangement when it is ready. Therefore, the correct order is C-D-A-B.

topic: Match the Following: focus on this supplied section: giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
Match each action with the quality it demonstrates. Each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) An editor removes unnecessary wording while retaining the essential points and uses few words.
(B) A writer arranges the ideas logically so that the explanation is clear.
(C) A coordinator is able to handle writing, editing and layout.
(D) A proofreader checks each correction carefully and correctly.

List-II
(I) Conscientious
(II) Concise
(III) Coherent
(IV) Versatile

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The editor’s action is concise because it retains necessary information and uses few words. The writer’s logical, clear arrangement is coherent; handling several kinds of work is versatile; and careful, correct checking is conscientious. These matches give (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

options: ["open and honest in saying what she thinks","aggressive or unfriendly and ready to argue or fight","hesitant to express an opinion firmly and confidently","able to recover quickly after something unpleasant"]

Isha’s reluctance to recommend a view contrasts with that meaning, making C the best antonym. Openness and honesty, hostility, and recovery after something unpleasant describe different qualities.

body: A company validly forfeits shares issued at a premium after a shareholder fails to pay a call. The full share premium had already been received and recorded before forfeiture, and no share premium is outstanding. What is the treatment of the recorded share-premium entry?
options: ["Reverse the share-premium entry along with the other entries for the forfeited shares.","Transfer the share premium received to Share Forfeiture A/c.","Leave the recorded share-premium entry unchanged.","Credit the share premium received to the unpaid call account."]
explanation: The stated accounting treatment reverses entries relating to forfeited shares except the entry for share premium received. Since the stem says the full premium was received and recorded before forfeiture, that entry remains unchanged.

In such circumstances, the company can forfeit their shares, i.e. cancel their allotment and treat the amount already received thereon as forfeited to the company within the framework of the provisions in its articles. These provisions are usually based on Table F which authorise the directors to forefeit the shares for non-payment of calls made. For this purpose, they have to strictly follow the procedure laid down in this regard. Following is the accounting treatment of shares issued at par, premium or at a discount. When shares are forefeited all entries relating to the shares forfeited except those relating to premium, already recorded in the accounting records must be reversed. Accordingly, share capital account is debited with the amount called-up in respect of shares are forfeited and crediting the respective unpaid calls accounts’s or calls in arrears account with the amount already received. This usually happens in respect of shares issue of well-managed and financially strong companies and is said to be a case of ‘Over Subscription’. In such a condition, three alternatives are available to the directors to deal with the situation: (1) they can accept some applications in full and totally reject the others; (2) they can make a pro-rata allotment to all; and (3) they can adopt a combination of the above two alternatives which happens to be the most common course adopted in practice. The problem of over subscription is resolved with the allotment of shares. Therefore, from the accounting point of view, it is better to place the situation of over subscription within the total frame of application and allotment, i.e. receipt of application amount, amount due on allotment and its receipt from the shareholders, and the same has been observed in the pattern of entries. First Alternative : When the directors decide to fully accept some applications and totally reject the others, the application money received on rejected applications is fully refunded. For example, a company invited applications for 20,000 shares and received the applications for 25,000 shares. The directors rejected the applications for 5,000 shares which are in excess of the required number and refunded their application money in full. body:
A company has 24,000 allotted shares on which a second and final call of ₹30 per share is due. Calls in advance of ₹1,80,000 are applicable to this call, and the entire remaining amount due is received in the bank. There are no other adjustments or receipts. How much is received in the bank for this call?
A. ₹7,20,000
B. ₹5,40,000
C. ₹9,00,000
D. ₹1,80,000
explanation: The total call due is 24,000 × ₹30 = ₹7,20,000. After adjusting ₹1,80,000 already standing as calls in advance, the bank receives ₹7,20,000 − ₹1,80,000 = ₹5,40,000.

body:
Four existing partners change their future profit-sharing ratio from 8:5:4:3 to 5:7:5:3, with no admission or retirement. The firm has goodwill, and only the goodwill adjustment arising from this ratio change is considered. Match each partner with the change in share and the corresponding goodwill-adjustment treatment.

List-I
(A) Partner A
(B) Partner B
(C) Partner C
(D) Partner D

List-II
(I) Loses 3/20; sacrificing partner, credited
(II) Gains 2/20; gaining partner, debited
(III) Gains 1/20; gaining partner, debited
(IV) Share unchanged; neither gaining nor sacrificing

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Both ratios total 20, so the partners’ shares can be compared using a denominator of 20. A’s share falls by 3/20, B’s rises by 2/20, C’s rises by 1/20, and D’s is unchanged. The sacrificing partner is credited and the gaining partners are debited in the goodwill adjustment, giving the mapping in option A.

body:
A company presents financial statements for two periods in comparative form. It applied different accounting principles in the two periods and has not disclosed this difference. Consider the following statements:
(A) The financial data are comparative despite the difference in accounting principles.
(B) The deviation in accounting principles should be mentioned in a footnote.
(C) Financial data are comparative only when the same accounting principles are used.
(D) A footnote makes the accounting principles used in the two periods the same.
Choose the correct answer:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (D) only","(B) and (C) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The data are comparative only when the same accounting principles are used, so statement (C) is correct. Since the principles differ, the deviation should be mentioned in a footnote, making statement (B) correct; disclosure does not make the principles used in the periods the same.

Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector. 4.4 Tools of Analysis of Financial Statements The most commonly used techniques of financial analysis are as follows: 1. Comparative Statements: These are the statements showing the profitability and financial position of a firm for different periods of time in a comparative form to give an idea about the position of two or more periods. It usually applies to the two important financial statements, namely, balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared in a comparative form. The financial data will be comparative only when same accounting principles are used in preparing these statements. If this is not the case, the deviation in the use of accounting principles should be mentioned as a footnote. Comparative figures indicate the trend and direction of financial position and operating results. This analysis is also known as ‘horizontal analysis’. 2. Common Size Statements: These are the statements which indicate the relationship of different items of a financial statement with a common item by expressing each item as a percentage of that common item. The percentage thus calculated can be easily compared with the results of corresponding percentages of the previous year or of some other firms, as the numbers are brought to common base. Such statements also allow an analyst to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry. Thus, common size statements are useful, both, in intra-firm comparisons over different years and also in making inter-firm comparisons for the same year or for several years. body:
A company has authorised 12,000 shares of ₹10 each. It issues all 10,000 shares offered to the public. Applications are received for 9,000 shares, and those 9,000 shares are allotted. The company calls ₹6 per allotted share and receives ₹48,600 in total against this call. No other amount has been called or received. Arrange the following capital amounts from largest to smallest:
(I) Authorised capital
(II) Issued capital
(III) Subscribed capital
(IV) Called-up capital
(V) Paid-up capital
(VI) Uncalled capital
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The amounts are authorised capital ₹1,20,000, issued capital ₹1,00,000, subscribed capital ₹90,000, called-up capital ₹54,000, paid-up capital ₹48,600, and uncalled capital ₹36,000. The uncalled amount is the subscribed capital not yet called: ₹90,000 − ₹54,000. In descending order, the amounts correspond to (I), (II), (III), (IV), (V) and (VI).

The company cannot raise more than the amount of capital as specified in the Memorandum of Association. It is also called Nominal or Registered capital. The authorised capital can be increased or decreased as per the procedure laid down in the Companies Act. It should be noted that the company need not issue the entire authorised capital for public subscription at a time. Depending upon its requirement, it may issue share capital but in any case, it should not be more than the amount of authorised capital. • Issued Capital: It is that part of the authorised capital which is actually issued to the public for subscription including the shares allotted to vendors and the signatories to the company’s memorandum. The authorised capital which is not offered for public subscription is known as ‘unissued capital’. Unissued capital may be offered for public subscription at a later date. • Subscribed Capital: It is that part of the issued capital which has been actually subscribed by the public. When the shares offered for public subscription are subscribed fully by the public the issued capital and subscribed capital would be the same. It may be noted that ultimately, the subscribed capital may be equal to or less than issued capital. In case the number of shares subscribed is less than what is offered, the company allots only the number of shares for which subscription has been received. In case it is higher than what is offered, the allotment will be equal to the offer. In other words, the fact of over subscription is not reflected in the books. • Called up Capital: It is that part of the subscribed capital which has been called up on the shares, i.e., what the company has asked the shareholders to pay. The company may decide to call the entire amount or part of the face value of the shares, For example, if the face value (also called nominal value) of a share allotted is Rs. 10 and the company has called up only Rs. 7 per share, in that scenario, the called up capital is Rs. 7 per share. The remaining Rs. 3 may be collected from its shareholders as and when needed. • Paid up Capital: It is that portion of the called up capital which has been actually received from the shareholders. When the shareholders have paid all the called amount, the called up capital is the same to the paid up capital. If any of the shareholders has not paid amount on calls, such an amount may be called as ‘calls in arrears’. Therefore, paid up capital is equal to the called-up capital minus call in arrears. • Uncalled Capital: That portion of the subscribed capital which has not yet been called up. As stated earlier, the company may collect this amount any time when it needs further funds. body: A and B are the only partners in a firm and share profits in the ratio 3:2. No partner is admitted or retires. They agree to share future profits in the ratio 2:3. Goodwill is to be adjusted between them; only the direction of the capital-account entries is required. Which treatment is appropriate?
options: ["Debit A's capital account and credit B's capital account.","Credit both A's and B's capital accounts.","Debit both A's and B's capital accounts.","Credit A's capital account and debit B's capital account."]
explanation: A's share falls from 3/5 to 2/5, so A sacrifices 1/5; B's share rises from 2/5 to 3/5, so B gains 1/5. The goodwill adjustment credits the sacrificing partner and debits the gaining partner. Therefore, A's capital account is credited and B's is debited.

body: P and Q admit R as a partner. Their profit-sharing ratio is 3:2:3, respectively. The firm earns a profit of ₹2,40,000. P and Q guarantee R a minimum share of ₹1,00,000, and any deficiency in R’s share is to be borne by P and Q in their relative profit-sharing ratio of 3:2. No other adjustments apply. What is the final distribution of profit among P, Q and R?
explanation: Before applying the guarantee, P, Q and R’s shares are ₹90,000, ₹60,000 and ₹90,000. R’s share is ₹10,000 below the guaranteed minimum; P bears ₹6,000 and Q bears ₹4,000 in the stated 3:2 ratio. Their final shares are therefore ₹84,000, ₹56,000 and ₹1,00,000, respectively.

body:
A company has received an amount from a shareholder before the relevant call is made. The amount remains unadjusted until that call becomes due. Match each event or question in List-I with the corresponding treatment in List-II.

List-I
(A) Receipt of the amount before the call is made
(B) Adjustment of the advance when the relevant call becomes due
(C) Balance-sheet presentation of the unadjusted amount
(D) Treatment of the amount in determining paid-up capital

List-II
(I) Show separately under Equity and Liabilities, under current liabilities, as ‘others current liabilities’
(II) Debit Bank A/c and credit Calls in Advance A/c
(III) Do not add the amount to paid-up capital
(IV) Debit Calls in Advance A/c and credit the Particular Call A/c

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: On receipt of calls in advance, Bank A/c is debited and Calls in Advance A/c is credited. When the call becomes due, Calls in Advance A/c is debited and the Particular Call A/c is credited. The unadjusted balance is shown separately under current liabilities as ‘others current liabilities’, and it is not added to paid-up capital.

The amount so received from the shareholders is known as “Calls in Advance”. The amount received in advance is a liability of the company and should be credited to ‘Call in Advance Account.” The amount received will be adjusted towards the payment of calls as and when they becomes due. Table F of the Companies Act provides for the payment of interest on calls in advance at a rate not exceeding 12% per annum. The following journal entry is recorded for the amount of calls received in advance. Bank A/c Dr. To Calls in Advance A/c (Amount received on call in advance) On the due date of the calls, the amount of ‘Calls in Advance’ is adjusted by the following entry : Calls in Advance A/c Dr. To Particular Call A/c (Calls in advance adjusted with the call money due) The balance in ‘Calls in Advance’ account is shown as a separate item under the title Equity and Liabilities in the company’s balance sheet under the head ‘current liabilities’, as sub-head ‘others current liabilities’. It is not added to the amount of paid-up capital. As ‘Calls in Advance’ is a liability of the company, it is under obligation, if provided by the Articles, to pay interest on such amount from the date of its receipt up to the date when appropriate call is due for payment. A stipulation is generally made in the Articles regarding the rate at which interest is payable. However, if Articles are silent on this account, Table F is applicable which provides for interest on calls in advance at a rate not exceeding 12% per annum. This usually happens in respect of shares issue of well-managed and financially strong companies and is said to be a case of ‘Over Subscription’. body:
Consider the following statements about common-size statements:
(A) In a common-size balance sheet, liabilities are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
(B) A common-size statement prepared for successive periods can show changes in the respective percentages over time.
(C) Common-size analysis can help compare enterprises that differ substantially in size by providing insight into the structure of their financial statements.
(D) In a common-size statement of profit and loss, expenditure items are expressed as a percentage of total assets.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(B) and (C) only","(A) and (D) only","(B) and (D) only"]
explanation: Statements (B) and (C) are correct: common-size statements for successive periods show changes in percentages, and common-size analysis can reveal financial-statement structure when comparing enterprises of substantially different sizes. Statement (A) is incorrect because liabilities are expressed as a percentage of total liabilities, not total assets. Statement (D) is incorrect because expenditure items in a common-size statement of profit and loss are expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations.

Here, each item in the statement is stated as a percentage of the aggregate, or revenue from operations of which that item is a part. For example, a common size balance sheet shows the percentage of each asset to the total assets, and that of each liability to the total liabilities. Similarly, in the common size statement of profit and loss, the items of expenditure are shown as a percentage of the revenue from operations. body:
A firm reports profits of ₹48,000, ₹56,000, ₹64,000 and ₹72,000 in four successive past years. The partners have agreed to value goodwill by the Average Profits Method at three years’ purchase. Treat average profit as the arithmetic mean of the four stated annual profits, with no other adjustment. Arrange the steps in the correct order to determine goodwill.
(A) Add the four annual profits.
(B) Divide their total by four to obtain average past profit.
(C) Multiply the average past profit by three.
(D) State the resulting amount as goodwill.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The total of the four profits is ₹2,40,000, giving an arithmetic average of ₹60,000. Applying the agreed three years’ purchase gives goodwill of ₹1,80,000, so the steps are to total the profits, calculate the average, multiply it and state the result.

body: A, B and C share profits in the ratio 4:3:2. N is admitted and receives a 1/5 share in the profits. The partners agree that N acquires this entire share from A, B and C in the ratio 2:1:1, respectively. This ratio specifies the proportions of N’s share contributed by A, B and C. What is the new profit-sharing ratio of A, B, C and N?
explanation: The agreed 2:1:1 ratio divides N’s 1/5 share into sacrifices of 1/10, 1/20 and 1/20 by A, B and C, respectively. Subtracting these from their original shares gives 31/90, 17/60 and 31/180; N receives 1/5. Using a common denominator of 180, the new ratio is 62:51:31:36.

body:
A deceased partner’s executor’s claim is being calculated. All amounts below are in rupees, represent the deceased partner’s amount or share where applicable, and are unpaid. All listed items apply, and no other items, payments or set-offs affect the claim.

Credit balance of capital account: ₹1,00,000
Credit balance of current account: ₹8,000
Share of goodwill: ₹15,000
Share of accumulated profits: ₹12,000
Share of gain on revaluation: ₹5,000
Share of profit up to the date of death: ₹9,000
Interest on capital up to the date of death: ₹4,000
Salary due up to the date of death: ₹3,000
Share of accumulated losses: ₹6,000
Drawings up to the date of death: ₹7,000
Interest on drawings up to the date of death: ₹1,000

What amount is due to the deceased partner’s executor?
explanation: The amounts included in the claim total ₹1,56,000, and the deductions total ₹14,000. Therefore, the amount due is ₹1,56,000 − ₹14,000 = ₹1,42,000. The accumulated losses, drawings and interest on drawings are deductions from the claim.

body:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) A non-financial company receives cash on disposal of machinery used as a fixed asset.
(B) A financial enterprise makes cash advances and loans to third parties as part of its operating activities.
(C) A company pays cash to acquire machinery for use as a fixed asset.
(D) A non-financial company makes a cash loan to a third party.
List-II
(I) Investing cash inflow from disposal of a fixed asset
(II) Operating cash flow from advances and loans made by a financial enterprise
(III) Investing cash outflow to acquire a fixed asset
(IV) Investing cash outflow for a loan or advance to a third party by a non-financial enterprise
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Cash received from disposing of a fixed asset is an investing inflow, while cash paid to acquire one is an investing outflow. A cash loan to a third party is an investing outflow, except that advances and loans made by a financial enterprise as part of its operating activities are operating cash flows. These classifications give the mapping in option B.

This is so because statement of profit and loss incorporates the effects of all operating activities of an enterprise. However, Statement of Profit and Loss is prepared on accrual basis (and not on cash basis). Moreover, it also includes certain non-operating items such as interest paid, profit/loss on sale of fixed assets, etc.) and non-cash items (such as depreciation, goodwill written-off, divident declared, etc. Therefore, it becomes necessary to adjust the amount of net profit/loss as shown by Statement of Profit and Loss for arriving at cash flows from operating activities. Let us look at the example : Statement of Profit and Loss Account for the year ended March 31, 2017 Particulars Note Figures in (Rs.) i) Revenue from Operations 1,00,000 ii) Other Income 1 2,000 iii) Total Revenues (i+ii) 1,02,000 iv) Expenses Cost of Materials Consumed 30,000 Purchases of stock-in-trade 10,000 Employees Benefits Expenses 10,000 Finance Costs 5,000 Depreciation 5,000 Other Expenses 12,000 72,000 v) Profit before Tax (iii-iv) 30,000 Note: Other income includes profit on sale of land. The above Statement of Profit and Loss shows the amount of net profit of Rs. 30,000. This has to be adjusted for arriving cash flows from operating activities. Let us take various items one by one. 1. Depreciation is a non-cash item and hence, Rs. 5,000 charged as depreciation does not result in any cash flow. Therefore, this amount must be added back to the net profit. 2. Finance costs of Rs. 5,000 is a cash outflow on account of financing activity. For an accounting year of 365 days, consider the average collection periods corresponding to trade receivables turnover ratios of 5 times (statements (A) and (C)) and 10 times (statements (B) and (D)). Which statements are correct?
(A) At a turnover ratio of 5 times, the average collection period is 73 days.
(B) At a turnover ratio of 10 times, the average collection period is 36.5 days.
(C) At a turnover ratio of 5 times, the average collection period is 1,825 days.
(D) At a turnover ratio of 10 times, the average collection period is 146 days.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (D) only","(B) and (C) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The average collection period is calculated as 365 divided by the trade receivables turnover ratio. Thus, 365 ÷ 5 = 73 days and 365 ÷ 10 = 36.5 days, so statements (A) and (B) are correct. The other stated periods do not follow from this calculation.

An analyst wants to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry using common-size statements. Arrange the following steps in a logical order.
(A) Compare the resulting percentages with corresponding percentages of the previous year or another firm.
(B) Express each financial-statement item as a percentage of the selected common item.
(C) Select a common item as the base.
(D) Use the percentage comparison to compare the companies’ operating and financing characteristics.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A common-size statement uses a common item as the base, so the base must be selected before each item is expressed as a percentage of it. The resulting percentages can then be compared with corresponding percentages from another firm or year. This comparison supports comparing the operating and financing characteristics of companies of different sizes in the same industry; therefore, the order is C-B-A-D.

Comparative Statements: These are the statements showing the profitability and financial position of a firm for different periods of time in a comparative form to give an idea about the position of two or more periods. It usually applies to the two important financial statements, namely, balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared in a comparative form. The financial data will be comparative only when same accounting principles are used in preparing these statements. If this is not the case, the deviation in the use of accounting principles should be mentioned as a footnote. Comparative figures indicate the trend and direction of financial position and operating results. This analysis is also known as ‘horizontal analysis’. 2. Common Size Statements: These are the statements which indicate the relationship of different items of a financial statement with a common item by expressing each item as a percentage of that common item. The percentage thus calculated can be easily compared with the results of corresponding percentages of the previous year or of some other firms, as the numbers are brought to common base. Such statements also allow an analyst to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry. A introduces a further ₹60,000 on 1 July; B withdraws ₹1,20,000 from capital on 1 October; and C introduces a further ₹60,000 on 1 December. The partnership deed expressly provides for interest on capital at 10% per annum for the financial year ending 31 March. There are no other capital changes. For this question, count whole months from the first day of each stated month through 31 March. What is the total interest on capital for the year?
explanation: A’s interest is ₹24,000 on opening capital plus ₹4,500 on the addition for 9 months, totalling ₹28,500. B’s interest is ₹15,000 on ₹3,00,000 for 6 months plus ₹9,000 on the remaining ₹1,80,000 for 6 months, totalling ₹24,000; C’s interest is ₹18,000 on opening capital plus ₹2,000 on the addition for 4 months, totalling ₹20,000. The total is ₹28,500 + ₹24,000 + ₹20,000 = ₹72,500.

body: A company issues one debenture with a nominal value of ₹2,400 for an issue price of ₹2,520. Which statement correctly describes the issue?
options: ["It is issued at a premium of ₹120.","It is issued at a discount of ₹120.","It is issued at a premium of ₹2,520.","It is issued at par."]
explanation: The issue price exceeds the nominal value by ₹2,520 − ₹2,400 = ₹120. A debenture is issued at a premium when its price is more than its nominal value, so the premium is ₹120.

body: A partnership is constituted for a fixed term ending on 30 June. Its business remains unfinished on that date. No contract extends the term or provides otherwise. What is the status of the firm when the fixed term expires?
options: ["The firm remains in existence until its business is completed.","The partnership ends, but the firm necessarily continues.","The firm is dissolved only if all partners consent to dissolution.","The firm is dissolved when the fixed term expires."]
explanation: For a firm constituted for a fixed term, expiry of that term dissolves the firm, subject to the partners’ contract. The stem states that no contract changes this result.

body:
A company forfeits 100 shares of ₹10 each, issued at par. The full ₹10 per share has been called up. Each shareholder paid ₹3 per share on application but did not pay the ₹2 per share allotment money or the ₹5 per share call money. No other amount is unpaid.

Match each account and entry direction in List-I with the amount to be recorded in the forfeiture entry in List-II.

List-I
(A) Share Capital A/c (Dr.)
(B) Share Forfeiture A/c (Cr.)
(C) Share Allotment A/c (Cr.)
(D) Share Calls A/c (Cr.)

List-II
(I) ₹1,000
(II) ₹300
(III) ₹200
(IV) ₹500

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Share Capital is debited with the called-up amount: 100 × ₹10 = ₹1,000. Share Forfeiture is credited with the amount received: 100 × ₹3 = ₹300. The unpaid allotment and call amounts are credited to their respective accounts: 100 × ₹2 = ₹200 and 100 × ₹5 = ₹500, respectively.

An analyst is reviewing the following features of common-size statements. Which combination of statements is correct?
(A) Each item in a common-size statement is expressed as a percentage of a common item.
(B) Common-size analysis is also known as horizontal analysis.
(C) Common-size statements can be used to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry.
(D) Common-size statements are useful for inter-firm comparisons but not for comparing different years within one firm.
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(B) and (C) only","(A) and (C) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: A common-size statement expresses each item as a percentage of a common item, and it can help compare companies of different sizes in the same industry. Common-size analysis is called vertical analysis, not horizontal analysis, and common-size statements are useful for comparisons within a firm across years as well as between firms.

Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector. 4.4 Tools of Analysis of Financial Statements The most commonly used techniques of financial analysis are as follows: 1. Comparative Statements: These are the statements showing the profitability and financial position of a firm for different periods of time in a comparative form to give an idea about the position of two or more periods. It usually applies to the two important financial statements, namely, balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared in a comparative form. The financial data will be comparative only when same accounting principles are used in preparing these statements. If this is not the case, the deviation in the use of accounting principles should be mentioned as a footnote. Comparative figures indicate the trend and direction of financial position and operating results. This analysis is also known as ‘horizontal analysis’. 2. Common Size Statements: These are the statements which indicate the relationship of different items of a financial statement with a common item by expressing each item as a percentage of that common item. The percentage thus calculated can be easily compared with the results of corresponding percentages of the previous year or of some other firms, as the numbers are brought to common base. Such statements also allow an analyst to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry. Thus, common size statements are useful, both, in intra-firm comparisons over different years and also in making inter-firm comparisons for the same year or for several years. body:
A firm's profits for its three past years were ₹36,000, ₹48,000 and ₹60,000. Take their arithmetic average as the past average profit. The agreed number of years' purchase is 4, and no adjustment to these figures is required. Arrange the actions for calculating goodwill under the Average Profits Method.
(A) Add the three annual profits.
(B) Divide their total by 3 to find the past average profit.
(C) Multiply the past average profit by 4 years' purchase.
(D) Record ₹1,92,000 as the goodwill.
Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: First, add the profits to get ₹1,44,000, then divide by 3 to obtain an average profit of ₹48,000. Multiplying ₹48,000 by 4 years' purchase gives goodwill of ₹1,92,000, so the correct sequence is (A)-(B)-(C)-(D).

body: At the admission of a new partner, P and Q are the only old partners and share profits in the ratio 3:2. During revaluation, the following changes are identified: an increase in an asset’s book value of ₹20,000; a decrease in another asset’s book value of ₹8,000; a decrease in liabilities of ₹2,000; an increase in other liabilities of ₹5,000; an unrecorded asset of ₹12,000; and an unrecorded liability of ₹4,000. These are the only revaluation items, and no other adjustment affects the Revaluation Account. What balance should the Revaluation Account show, and how should it be transferred to P and Q’s capital accounts?
options: ["Credit balance of ₹21,000; credit P’s Capital Account by ₹12,600 and Q’s by ₹8,400","Credit balance of ₹17,000; credit P’s Capital Account by ₹10,200 and Q’s by ₹6,800","Debit balance of ₹17,000; debit P’s Capital Account by ₹10,200 and Q’s by ₹6,800","Credit balance of ₹13,000; credit P’s Capital Account by ₹6,500 and Q’s by ₹6,500"]
explanation: Asset increases, liability decreases and unrecorded assets are credited to the Revaluation Account; asset decreases, liability increases and unrecorded liabilities are debited. Credits total ₹34,000 and debits total ₹17,000, so the account shows a credit balance of ₹17,000. This gain is transferred to P and Q in their old ratio of 3:2, giving P ₹10,200 and Q ₹6,800.

body: A sole-proprietary business is expanding and now needs more capital, a larger number of people to manage it, and a way to share its business risks. Which organisational form is usually adopted in this situation?
options: ["Partnership form of organisation","Sole-proprietary form of organisation","Company form of organisation","Co-operative form of organisation"]
explanation: The stated principle is that when an expanding business needs more capital, more people to manage it and a way to share its risks, people usually adopt the partnership form of organisation. Therefore, option A is correct.

body: At a service centre, a manager tells staff the service target, explains the tasks, guides and counsels employees who encounter difficulty, encourages them to contribute effort, and leads the team towards the target. Which interpretation best captures the manager's role in this situation?
options: ["The role is communication alone: explaining tasks is included, but guidance, counselling, motivation and leadership are outside directing.","The role is motivation alone: encouraging effort is included, but instruction, guidance, counselling and leadership are outside directing.","The role is directing as a combined process: instruction, guidance, counselling, motivation and leadership are included in pursuing the objective.","The role is leadership alone: leading the team is included, but instruction, guidance, counselling and motivation are outside directing."]
explanation: Directing involves instructing, guiding, counselling, motivating and leading people to achieve organisational objectives; it is not merely communication. The manager performs these activities towards the stated target, so the role is directing as a combined process.
supporting_excerpts: [{"id":"ncert-lebs107","locator":"normative-a72a9103340a296e","text":"In the context of management of an organisation, directing refers to the process of instructing, guiding, counselling, motivating and leading people in the organisation to achieve its objectives. You can observe here that directing is not a mere issue of communication but encompasses many elements like supervision, motivation and leadership. It is one of the key managerial functions performed by every manager. Directing is a managerial process which takes place throughout the life of an organisation. The main characteristics of directing are discussed below: (i) Directing initiates action: Directing is a key managerial function. A manager has to perform this function along with planning, organising, staffing and controlling while discharging his duties in the organisation. While other functions prepare a setting for action, directing initiates action in the organisation. (ii) Directing takes place at every level of management: Every manager, from top executive to supervisor performs the function of directing. The directing takes place wherever superior – subordinate relations exist. (iii) Directing is a continuous process: Directing is a continuous activity. It takes place throughout the life of the organisation irrespective of people occupying managerial positions. We can observe that in organisations like Infosys, Tata, BHEL, HLL and the managers may change but the directing process continues because without direction the organisational activities can not continue further. (iv) Directing flows from top to bottom: Directing is first initiated at top level and flows to the bottom through organisational hierarchy.","url":"https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebs107.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":"NCERT Business Studies I, Chapter 7: Directing, reprint 2026–27","kind":"reference"},{"id":"ncert-lebs107","locator":"normative-34f28c2e46790f5a","text":"For example, a good motivation plan with suitable monetary and non-monetary rewards can motivate an employee to contribute his maximum efforts for the organisation as he or she may feel that their efforts will bring them suitable rewards. (ii) Harmony of objectives: Very often, we find that individual objectives of employees and the organisational objectives as understood are conflicting to each other. For example, an employee may expect attractive salary and monetary benefits to fulfill his personal needs. The organisation may expect employees to improve productivity to achieve expected profits. But, good directing should provide harmony by convincing that employee rewards and work efficiency are complimentary to each other. (iii) Unity of Command: This principle insists that a person in the organisation should receive instructions from one superior only. If instructions are received from more than one, it creates confusion, conflict and disorder in the organisation. Adherence to this principle ensures effective direction. (iv) Appropriateness of direction tech­ nique: According to this principle, appropriate motivational and leadership technique should be used while directing the people based on subordinate needs, capabilities, attitudes and other situational variables. For example, for some people money can act as powerful motivator while for others promotion may act as effective motivator. (v) Managerial communication: Effe- ctive managerial communication across all the levels in the organisation makes direction effective. Directing should convey clear instructions to create total understanding to subordinates.","url":"https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebs107.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":"NCERT Business Studies I, Chapter 7: Directing, reprint 2026–27","kind":"reference"}]

topic: Financial Markets: focus on this supplied section: One of the main objectives of the primary market is to allow companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities. Test a distinct implication, application or calculation supported by it.
body:
Consider the following independent cases:
(A) Company M issues securities and raises capital through that issuance.
(B) Company N issues securities, but the issuance raises no capital for the company.
(C) Company P raises capital by issuing securities.
(D) Company Q raises capital through a loan and does not issue securities.
Which cases illustrate the primary market objective of allowing companies to raise capital through the issuance of securities?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(B) and (D) only","(A) and (C) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The stated objective is illustrated when a company raises capital through issuing securities, as in cases (A) and (C). In (B), the issuance raises no capital for the company; in (D), the company raises capital but does not issue securities.

body:
A firm is establishing a control procedure for one key result area. The manager must set up the procedure and then handle a deviation that qualifies for managerial attention. Arrange the following stages from earliest to latest:
(A) Set the critical point and permissible limit for the key result area.
(B) Identify a deviation that requires managerial attention by assessing it against the permissible limit.
(C) Bring the significant deviation beyond the permissible limit to management’s notice.
(D) Analyse the causes of the deviation requiring managerial attention.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The manager first establishes the critical point and permissible limit, then identifies which deviation requires attention. A deviation beyond that limit is brought to management’s notice, and the identified deviation is then analysed for its causes. The other sequences place identification before setting the limit, notification before confirming the deviation qualifies, or cause analysis before notification.

body: A manager observes that employees have completed their separate assignments, but their efforts are directed towards conflicting priorities and are not contributing to the department’s shared target. The manager explains how each person’s work should connect with colleagues’ contributions and the organisational target. Which importance of directing is most directly illustrated?
options: ["Initiating action towards the attainment of desired objectives","Integrating individual efforts so they contribute to organisational performance","Enabling employees to realise their potential through motivation and effective leadership","Ensuring that instructions are implemented in the proper perspective"]
explanation: The manager links individual contributions so they work together towards an organisational target. This illustrates the integration of employee efforts, through which individual effort contributes to organisational performance. The focus is on connecting existing efforts, rather than initiating action or motivating employees to realise their potential.

body: A securities-desk trainee is classifying share transactions. In each record, the named seller or transferor is the person from whom the recipient obtains the shares. Which record belongs to the secondary market?
options: ["A retail investor buys shares directly from the issuing company.","A retail investor buys shares already held by another investor.","A retail investor receives shares from another investor as a gift, with no payment.","A retail investor sells shares directly to the issuing company."]
explanation: In option B, the buyer obtains shares from another investor, which fits the definition of the secondary market. Option A involves the issuing company as seller, while option C is a gift rather than a purchase or sale.

body:
A business has vacancies and is considering candidates from its existing workforce as well as candidates from outside. It seeks fresh talent and a wider choice of candidates. Consider the following statements:
(A) External sources of recruitment are used to obtain fresh talent and a wider choice.
(B) Recruitment from within the enterprise is internal recruitment.
(C) Transfers and promotions are important sources of internal recruitment.
(D) Recruitment from within the enterprise is external recruitment.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A), (B) and (D) only","(A), (C) and (D) only","(A), (B) and (C) only","(B), (C) and (D) only"]
explanation: External sources are used when fresh talent and a wider choice are sought. Recruitment from within the enterprise is internal recruitment, and transfers and promotions are important internal sources. Statement (D) reverses the distinction between internal and external recruitment; therefore, statements (A), (B) and (C) are correct.

Match List-I with List-II by pairing each business-environment change with the effect associated with it.
List-I
(A) Increase in taxes by government
(B) Technological improvements
(C) Political uncertainty
(D) Changes in fashions and tastes of consumers
List-II
(I) May create fear in the minds of investors
(II) May render existing products obsolete
(III) May make things expensive to buy
(IV) May shift demand from existing products to new ones
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: An increase in government taxes may make things expensive to buy, while technological improvements may render existing products obsolete. Political uncertainty may create fear among investors, and changes in fashions and tastes may shift demand from existing products to new ones; therefore, the correct matching is option A.

Riya is selecting a household product and will then use it. Arrange the following consumer responsibilities in the order that moves from making an informed market choice to selecting a product and then using it safely.
(A) Be aware of the goods and services available in the market so that an intelligent and wise choice can be made.
(B) Buy only standardised goods.
(C) Learn about risks associated with the product, follow the manufacturer’s instructions and use it safely.
Choose the correct order from the options given below:
explanation: The progression is from awareness of available goods and services to choosing standardised goods, and then to learning about risks and using the product safely. Therefore, the order is (A)-(B)-(C), which is option D.

body: A firm has designated process temperature as a critical point. Its standard is 80°C, and the permissible variation is ±2°C. The current deviation from the standard is +6°C, which the firm classifies as major. All other tracked measures are within their permissible ranges. Which action best follows the firm’s control arrangement?
options: ["Leave the +6°C deviation to routine handling unless another critical measure also deviates.","Forward every tracked observation, including within-limit readings, for equal-priority management review.","Bring the +6°C deviation at the critical point to management for immediate priority action.","Record the +6°C deviation but defer management action until the next review cycle."]
explanation: The +6°C deviation is outside the stated ±2°C permissible range, and the firm has identified process temperature as a critical point. The excerpt states that a major deviation at a critical point calls for immediate action on a priority basis.

body: At a manufacturing unit, the plant manager sends two shift supervisors the same message, which only reports the organisational output objective and gives no task instructions. Supervisor X gives the team work instructions, guides task performance, counsels a hesitant worker, motivates the team and leads its effort towards the objective. Supervisor Y forwards the message verbatim and has no further interaction with the team. Considering each supervisor’s interaction with the respective shift team, which assessment best applies the meaning of directing?
options: ["Supervisor X’s interaction is directing beyond communication, while Supervisor Y’s interaction is communication of the objective alone.","Both interactions are directing, because communicating an organisational objective is sufficient by itself.","Neither interaction is directing, because guidance, counselling, motivation and leadership are separate from directing.","Only Supervisor Y’s interaction is directing, because the objective message is direction whereas Supervisor X’s additional activities are separate functions."]
explanation: Supervisor X’s instructions, guidance, counselling, motivation and leadership are elements of directing. Supervisor Y only relays the objective, and directing is not merely communication.

You can observe here that directing is not a mere issue of communication but encompasses many elements like supervision, motivation and leadership. It is one of the key managerial functions performed by every manager. Directing is a managerial process which takes place throughout the life of an organisation. The main characteristics of directing are discussed below: (i) Directing initiates action: Directing is a key managerial function. A manager has to perform this function along with planning, organising, staffing and controlling while discharging his duties in the organisation. While other functions prepare a setting for action, directing initiates action in the organisation. (ii) Directing takes place at every level of management: Every manager, from top executive to supervisor performs the function of directing. The directing takes place wherever superior – subordinate relations exist. (iii) Directing is a continuous process: Directing is a continuous activity. It takes place throughout the life of the organisation irrespective of people occupying managerial positions. We can observe that in organisations like Infosys, Tata, BHEL, HLL and the managers may change but the directing process continues because without direction the organisational activities can not continue further. (iv) Directing flows from top to bottom: Directing is first initiated at top level and flows to the bottom through organisational hierarchy.","url":"https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebs107.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":"NCERT Business Studies I, Chapter 7: Directing, reprint 2026–27","kind":"reference"},{"id":"ncert-lebs107","locator":"normative-34f28c2e46790f5a","text":"For example, a good motivation plan with suitable monetary and non-monetary rewards can motivate an employee to contribute his maximum efforts for the organisation as he or she may feel that their efforts will bring them suitable rewards. (ii) Harmony of objectives: Very often, we find that individual objectives of employees and the organisational objectives as understood are conflicting to each other. For example, an employee may expect attractive salary and monetary benefits to fulfill his personal needs. The organisation may expect employees to improve productivity to achieve expected profits. But, good directing should provide harmony by convincing that employee rewards and work efficiency are complimentary to each other. (iii) Unity of Command: This principle insists that a person in the organisation should receive instructions from one superior only. If instructions are received from more than one, it creates confusion, conflict and disorder in the organisation. Adherence to this principle ensures effective direction. (iv) Appropriateness of direction tech­ nique: According to this principle, appropriate motivational and leadership technique should be used while directing the people based on subordinate needs, capabilities, attitudes and other situational variables. For example, for some people money can act as powerful motivator while for others promotion may act as effective motivator. (v) Managerial communication: Effe- ctive managerial communication across all the levels in the organisation makes direction effective. Directing should convey clear instructions to create total understanding to subordinates.","url":"https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebs107.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":"NCERT Business Studies I, Chapter 7: Directing, reprint 2026–27","kind":"reference"}]

body:
Consider the following transactions. Each transaction concerns shares or securities; the individuals are investors, and the company described as issuing the shares is the issuer.
(A) Meera buys shares from another individual investor.
(B) An issuing company sells shares directly to Meera.
(C) Meera sells securities to another individual investor.
(D) Meera sells shares directly to the company that issued them.
Which of the following statements describe transactions in the secondary market?
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(B) and (D) only","(C) and (D) only","(A) and (C) only"]
explanation: A secondary-market transaction is a purchase or sale of shares or securities between investors, rather than with the issuer. In (A) and (C), both parties are investors; the company is the issuer in (B) and (D).

List-I
(A) Human relations approach
(B) Prime concern of the staffing function
(C) Staffing in relation to positions in the organisation structure
(D) Staffing as a job-person matching function
List-II
(I) Timely fulfilment of manpower requirements
(II) Recognition of the human factor as the most important instrument of success in an organisation
(III) Filling the positions provided for in the organisation structure
(IV) Finding the right people for the right job

explanation: The human relations approach recognises the human factor as important to organisational success, while the staffing function’s prime concern is timely fulfilment of manpower requirements. Staffing also fills the positions in the organisation structure and finds the right people for the right job, so the complete matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

(A) The regulation requires the statutory warning in the advertisement.
(B) The advertiser omits the required warning.

(D) The business may face legal problems due to non-compliance.

explanation: The requirement comes first; under the stated assumption, omitting the warning makes the advertisement non-compliant. Non-compliance can lead to legal problems, so that possible consequence follows the non-compliance.

body: A quality-control manager has set a standard of no more than 6 defective units per 1,000 units produced. During one shift, 2,400 units are produced and 12 are defective. Assume the 2,400 units are the full output covered by the standard for that shift, and the 12 defective units are the complete count for that output. Which comparison of actual performance with the standard is correct?
options: ["The actual rate is 12 defects per 1,000 units, exceeding the standard by 6 per 1,000.","The actual rate is 0.5 defects per 1,000 units, below the standard by 5.5 per 1,000.","The actual rate is 5 defects per 1,000 units, exceeding the standard by 1 per 1,000.","The actual rate is 5 defects per 1,000 units, below the standard by 1 per 1,000."]
explanation: The actual rate per 1,000 units is (12 ÷ 2,400) × 1,000 = 5. The standard is 6 defects per 1,000 units, so the actual rate is 1 defect per 1,000 below the standard. Expressing both figures in the same units makes the comparison direct.

body:
A person who obtains goods or avails services for resale or commercial purpose is not treated as a consumer and is outside the scope of consumer protection. Match each case in List-I with the classification in List-II. For (C) and (D), neither resale nor commercial purpose applies; the classification must not imply any other eligibility.
List-I
(A) A shopkeeper obtains goods solely to resell them.
(B) A company avails a service solely for its commercial operations.
(C) A household obtains goods solely for household use, not for resale or commercial purpose.
(D) An individual avails a service solely for personal use, not for resale or commercial purpose.
List-II
(I) Goods obtained for resale; the stated purpose falls within the exclusion.
(II) Services availed for commercial purpose; the stated purpose falls within the exclusion.
(III) Goods obtained for neither resale nor commercial purpose; the stated purpose does not fall within this exclusion.
(IV) Services availed for neither resale nor commercial purpose; the stated purpose does not fall within this exclusion.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
B. (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
C. (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
D. (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
explanation: Goods obtained for resale and services availed for commercial purpose fall within the stated exclusion. The household goods and personal service in (C) and (D) are expressly not for resale or commercial purpose, so those stated uses do not fall within this exclusion. This matching classifies only the stated purpose and does not establish any other eligibility.

body: A manager faces a workplace situation and consults management principles before choosing a course of action and putting it into effect. Which statement best describes the role of those principles in this situation?
options: ["They provide general guidelines for workplace conduct and help managers take and implement decisions.","They specify the benefits of management principles, such as efficiency and optimum utilisation of resources.","They describe the nature of management principles, including flexibility and contingency.","They state Taylor’s principles of scientific management, such as cooperation and maximum output."]
explanation: Management principles are general guidelines that can be used in workplace situations and help managers take and implement decisions. Option B describes their significance, option C describes their nature, and option D names Taylor’s scientific-management principles.

He also suggested that managers should have the following qualities- Physical; Moral; Education; Knowledge; and Experience. body:
An organisation has two vacancies. Its HR team identifies people who may be suitable and circulates vacancy notices inviting them to apply. After applications are received, the team compares candidates for the jobs. Which activity in the case represents recruitment?
A. Identifying prospective employees and stimulating them to apply
B. Assessing applicants and making the final match
C. Acquainting employees with work and developing their skills
D. Shifting an employee between jobs without a substantive change in responsibilities and status
options: ["Identifying prospective employees and stimulating them to apply","Assessing applicants and making the final match","Acquainting employees with work and developing their skills","Shifting an employee between jobs without a substantive change in responsibilities and status"]
explanation: Recruitment involves searching for prospective employees and stimulating them to apply. Comparing candidates is selection, while acquainting employees with work and developing their skills is training. Shifting an employee between jobs as described is a transfer.

body:
At a company, the senior-most executives include managers heading finance and marketing. Consider the following statements about its top management:
(A) Top management coordinates departmental activities according to each department’s own objectives rather than the organisation’s overall objectives.
(B) Top management analyses the business environment and its implications for the firm’s survival.
(C) Top management implements and controls plans and strategies formulated by middle management.
(D) Top management formulates overall organisational goals and strategies for their achievement.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (C) only","(B) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only"]
explanation: Top management analyses the business environment and its implications for the firm’s survival, and formulates overall organisational goals and strategies for their achievement. Therefore, statements (B) and (D) are correct. Statement (A) reverses the stated basis for coordinating departments, while statement (C) assigns top management the implementation and control role stated for middle management.

body:
A company is organising its work through four separate decisions. Match each decision in List-I with the corresponding step in the organising process in List-II.
List-I
(A) Before deciding departments or job-holders, management breaks the total workload into identifiable activities.
(B) Activities with related features are grouped into departments, without yet naming the employees who will perform them.
(C) After the departments have been settled, specified duties are allotted to particular employees.
(D) For each position, the direct superior to whom its holder reports is recorded.
List-II
(I) Identification and division of work
(II) Departmentalisation
(III) Assignment of Duties
(IV) Establishing reporting relationships
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Breaking the workload into identifiable activities is identification and division of work, while grouping related activities into departments is departmentalisation. Allocating specified duties to employees is assignment of duties; recording who reports to whom establishes reporting relationships. Thus, option B gives the correct one-to-one matching.

Organisational structure is the framework within which managerial and operating tasks are performed. It can be functional or divisional. Span of management is the number of subordinates under a superior. Functional structure groups activities on the basis of functions. The advantages of such a structure are specialisation, better control, managerial efficiency and ease in training employees. The disadvantages are functional empires, conflict of interest, inflexibility, and restriction in managerial development. Divisional structure groups activities on the basis of products. The advantages are integration, product specialisation, greater accountability, flexibility, better coordination and more initiative. The disadvantages are departmental conflicts, costly process, ignoring of organisational interests, increase in requirements of general managers. Formal organisation is designed by the management to achieve organisational goals. Its advantages are fixation of responsibility, clarity of roles, unity of command and effective accomplishment of goals. Its disadvantages are procedural delays, inadequate recognition of creativity, limited in scope. Informal organisation arises out of interaction amongst people at work. Its advantages are speed, fulfillment of social needs, fills inadequacies of formal structure. Its disadvantages are: disruptive force, resistance to change and priority to group interests. body: A group of 48 workers takes temporary jobs in an urban area. Five-eighths of the group take these jobs, remain there for 3 months, and then return to their home villages; the remaining workers do not take urban jobs. Count one worker employed for one month as one worker-month. How many worker-months of urban employment does the group record during this spell?
options: ["90 worker-months","144 worker-months","30 worker-months","54 worker-months"]
explanation: The number taking urban jobs is 48 × 5/8 = 30. Their urban employment totals 30 × 3 = 90 worker-months. The calculation counts only the workers who take urban jobs and uses their stated three-month stay.

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Household use of wood, dung cake or other biomass as fuel
(B) LPG used as a household fuel
(C) Material fed into a gobar gas plant
(D) Material left after gas production

List-II
(I) Cattle dung
(II) A clean fuel that reduces household pollution to a large extent and minimises wastage
(III) Slurry that is a good organic fertiliser and soil conditioner
(IV) A practice associated with deforestation, reduction in green cover and air pollution

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The use of wood, dung cake or other biomass as household fuel is linked to deforestation, reduced green cover and air pollution, while LPG reduces household pollution and minimises wastage. Cattle dung is fed into a gobar gas plant, and the slurry left over is a good organic fertiliser and soil conditioner; therefore, the correct mapping is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

(A) The faster human-capital growth caused the slower growth of per-capita real income.
(B) The growth rates alone do not establish a cause-and-effect relation between human-capital growth and economic growth.
(C) The slower growth of per-capita real income establishes that human capital made no contribution to economic growth.
(D) The faster human-capital growth establishes that it raised per-capita real-income growth.
options: ["Statement (A) only","Statement (B) only","Statement (C) only","Statement (D) only"]

Therefore, the two growth rates alone do not establish that human capital caused slower growth, made no contribution, or raised per-capita real-income growth.

(A) Farmers may view a new technology as risky.

body: Two cooperatives report annual fish-production values of ₹48 lakh and ₹72 lakh. For this exercise, treat the source shares as exact: inland sources together account for 75% of each cooperative’s total value, and the marine sector accounts for the remaining 25%. Each cooperative divides its inland-source value equally between river-sourced and lake-sourced fish; all marine-sector value is sea-sourced. What are the combined values attributed to river, lake and sea across both cooperatives, respectively?

body: A report notes that Country P’s economic growth is relatively strong compared with other developing countries. It also records little progress in Country P’s human development indicators. The author claims that the first finding is enough to demonstrate considerable progress in human development. Which evaluation is best supported?
options: ["Reject the claim because relatively strong economic growth alone does not establish considerable progress in human development.","Accept the claim because relatively strong economic growth establishes considerable progress in human development.","Reject the claim because little progress in human development establishes that economic growth was relatively weak.","Accept the claim because human development indicators need not be considered when economic growth is relatively strong."]
explanation: The reported growth performance and the reported human development indicators are distinct findings. Relatively strong economic growth alone does not establish that considerable progress has been made in human development.

Count jobs in the steel company as direct employment and jobs in the purchasing enterprises as indirect employment. Assume there are no other employment changes. How many jobs are generated in total?

explanation: The steel company creates 24 direct jobs, while the purchasing enterprises create 5 + 7 + 9 = 21 indirect jobs. The total is 24 + 21 = 45 jobs.

body:
Match each description in List I with the formulation or consequence in List II that it expresses.

List-I
(A) A proposal meets the present generation’s needs while preserving future generations’ ability to meet their own needs.
(B) A programme meets the basic needs of all and gives all an opportunity to fulfil their aspirations for a better life.
(C) A programme directly focuses on increasing the material standard of living of poor people.
(D) A development path enhances current living styles without concern for posterity, with resource depletion and environmental degradation as the stated consequence.

List-II
(I) Edward Barbier’s stated focus
(II) Consequence of development without concern for posterity
(III) UNCED formulation
(IV) Our Common Future formulation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The present-needs and future-capacity criterion is the UNCED formulation, while the Our Common Future formulation describes meeting everyone’s basic needs and extending to all the opportunity to fulfil their aspirations. Barbier’s stated focus is increasing the material standard of living of the poor. Development without concern for posterity is stated to deplete resources and degrade the environment, so the mapping in option (A) is correct.

The following statements present reasons for the extensive role of governments in promoting the industrial sector.
(A) Industrialists did not have the capital to invest in industrial ventures required for the development of the Indian economy.
(B) The market was not large enough to encourage industrialists to undertake major projects.
(C) This market constraint applied even when industrialists had the capital to undertake those projects.
(D) It was principally for these reasons that the erstwhile governments had to play an extensive role in promoting the industrial sector.
Arrange the statements in the order in which the rationale proceeds. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The rationale first states that industrialists lacked the capital for the required industrial investment, then adds that the market was too small to encourage major projects. The phrase “even if they had the capital” qualifies that market constraint, and the extensive government role follows as the response to these reasons. Thus, the order is A-B-C-D.

body:
A consumer records the following optimal purchases of bananas. The prices of all other goods are the same in every period.
Period I: Price of bananas ₹10 per unit; monthly income ₹30,000; tastes and preferences P; quantity chosen 4 units.
Period II: Price of bananas ₹12 per unit; monthly income ₹30,000; tastes and preferences P; quantity chosen 3 units.
Period III: Price of bananas ₹10 per unit; monthly income ₹40,000; tastes and preferences P; quantity chosen 6 units.
Period IV: Price of bananas ₹12 per unit; monthly income ₹30,000; tastes and preferences Q, which differ from P; quantity chosen 5 units.
Which pair of periods can be compared to examine the relationship between the price of bananas and the quantity chosen while keeping the other demand determinants unchanged?
options: ["Periods I and III","Periods II and III","Periods I and II","Periods II and IV"]
explanation: A demand curve relates price to the quantity optimally chosen when prices of other goods, income, and tastes and preferences remain unchanged. Only between Periods I and II do those other determinants stay the same while the banana price differs.

Match List-I with List-II. Use the stated motivations and relations to classify each entry.
List-I
(A) An international sale is made to earn profit and is independent of any BoP gap.
(B) An international transaction is determined by the gap left by autonomous transactions.
(C) Autonomous receipts exceed autonomous payments.
(D) Autonomous receipts are less than autonomous payments.
List-II
(I) BoP deficit
(II) Autonomous transaction (“above the line”)
(III) Accommodating transaction (“below the line”)
(IV) BoP surplus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The profit-motivated sale, being independent of the BoP gap, is autonomous; the transaction determined by the gap is accommodating. Autonomous receipts greater than payments indicate a BoP surplus, while receipts less than payments indicate a BoP deficit. Thus, the correct mapping is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV) and (D)-(I).
